The business already had a PIM when the current team arrived, but nobody knew how it had been configured and an upgrade changed nothing. The team switched off its intergrations to the websote and managed product content directly in thr SAP Commerce back office instead. The replacement project then ran through a group-level change of ownership staffed by three people.

Product structure made it harder. A physiotherapy couch available in 32 colours was listed as one product, because only one person in. the business knew how to build variants in SAP Commerce. Missing GTINs had products banned from Google Shopping and finding them meant exporting 25,000 SKUs to a spreadsheet, filtering by hand, then re-importing.

The deciding factor was who would actually use it. Vital Healthcare put the shortlisted platforms in front of around five people in the web team, twenty in the commercial team and five in IT. The web team had a preference on interface design, but the commercial team had already failed to adopt the SAP Commerce back office, and they found Pimberly the easier system to work in.

Attribute modelling carried most of the work. Vital Healthcare worked through manufacturer specification sheets to establish what data data existed for medical equipment and chose to build more attributes than the team needed on day one rather than fewer. The build settled at nearly 400 attributes and over 100 taxonomy nodes across three tiers, and five category trees.
